MCP Penalty on a Block of Coefficients

Source: R/penalized_ctors.R
mcp.Rd

Specifies the minimax concave penalty. Like SCAD it selects and then flattens, and it begins to flatten immediately, whereas SCAD keeps the slope of the lasso up to \(t = \lambda\).

Usage

mcp(
  x,
  label = "mcp",
  standardize = FALSE,
  lambda = NULL,
  gamma = 3,
  id = NULL,
  n_lambda = 25,
  n_gamma = 5,
  min_ratio = 1e-04,
  search = "grid",
  sparse = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A one-sided formula, such as ~ x1 + x2 or ~ 0 + g, or a numeric matrix, ideally a matrix column of the model data frame. A two-sided formula is rejected with an error.

label

A single non-empty character string prefixed to the coefficient names as label.name, "mcp" by default, so a block over x1 reads mcp.x1. Two penalized terms in one formula stay apart by their labels.

standardize

A single logical, FALSE by default: whether to penalize each coefficient on the scale of its own column. See the section above.

lambda

The scale of the penalty. One number holds it, several are the grid that the path visits as they stand, and NULL, the default, has the path build one. Must lie in \((0, \infty)\).

gamma

The shape, in the same three states and settled independently of lambda, defaulting to the literature's 3 rather than to NULL: one number holds it, several are the grid that the path visits as they stand, and NULL has the path build one. Must lie in \((1, \infty)\).

id

Labels sharing this term's hyperparameters with those of other terms carrying the same ones: each is then estimated at a single value, wherever in the formula they sit. The argument is a named vector, c(gamma = "A"), because the penalty has several hyperparameters and the name identifies the one that is shared; NULL, the default, shares nothing. See term_ids() for the meaning of the labels and the restrictions on their use.

n_lambda, n_gamma

The number of values that the path visits for each, at least 2. The two are separate arguments because the axes differ: \(\lambda\) descends from the kink size that empties the block to min_ratio times that size (four decades at the default min_ratio), which takes more points than \(\gamma\), which spans the shape's useful range. Each signals an error when given explicitly for a hyperparameter that is held or written out, so n_gamma requires gamma = NULL.

min_ratio

How far down the path reaches, as a fraction of the kink that empties the block: smaller reaches a denser fit, larger stops sooner. It is a single number in \((0, 1)\), 1e-4 by default. Only the sweep by kink size reads it, and it signals an error when given explicitly while lambda is held or written out.

search

"grid" to visit every combination of \(\lambda\) and \(\gamma\), "cyclic" to sweep one at a time while the other is held. See term_search(). Given explicitly while fewer than two hyperparameters are swept, it signals an error.

sparse

Governs the formula route: TRUE builds a dgCMatrix through Matrix::sparse.model.matrix(), FALSE a dense model matrix, and NULL, the default, settles it at build from the size of the design. A matrix input needs no such argument. See the section above.

...

Not used. Any argument supplied here is rejected with an error that names it and lists the penalty's hyperparameters. The typical case is an argument named after another penalty's hyperparameter: scad(~ x, gamma = 1) signals "'scad' has no argument 'gamma'.".

Value

An unbuilt PenalizedTerm(): a specification whose X, coef_names, blueprint and penalty are empty until term_build() fills them. The build attaches the penalty over the block's columns.

Details

The penalty is defined by its derivative, for \(t = \lvert\beta_j\rvert \ge 0\), $$\rho'(t) = \left(\lambda - \frac{t}{\gamma}\right)_+ ,$$ summed over the coefficients: it starts at \(\lambda\), falls linearly, and is flat past \(t = \gamma\lambda\). The penalty is improper, so it carries no normalizing constant and is not reachable by a marginal criterion.

The formula above is the penalty for a loss of unit curvature. In a statmodels7::statmod() fit the penalty on coordinate \(j\) is scaled by the curvature \(c_j\) of the likelihood in that coordinate: the slope at zero remains \(\lambda\), and the penalty is flat past \(\gamma\lambda/c_j\), so the shape keeps its meaning whatever the scale of the response. Rescaling a Gaussian response by \(k\) and dividing \(\lambda\) by \(k\) reproduces the fit, in which \(\gamma\) is unchanged. The scaling is applied by statmodels7; the penalty that this term builds is the unscaled one.

The hyperparameters are lambda, on \((0, \infty)\), swept over n_lambda values by kink size, and gamma, on \((1, \infty)\). At or below 1 the penalized objective need not be convex even for an orthogonal design. The shape leaves the kink at zero unchanged, so a path over the kink size cannot reach it. It is swept over n_gamma values on a geometric grid that starts just above the smallest shape at which the block can be fitted.

The shape is held at \(\gamma = 3\) by default, the value that ncvreg holds, so only \(\lambda\) is searched. gamma = NULL estimates it over the grid instead, and n_gamma sizes that grid. The grid runs from 0.25 to 25 above the smallest admissible shape.

References

Zhang, C.-H. (2010). Nearly unbiased variable selection under minimax concave penalty. The Annals of Statistics 38, 894–942.

See also

penalized_terms() for what the five share, ridge(), lasso(), enet(), scad(), penalties7::mcp_penalty()

Examples

set.seed(3)
dd <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(20), x2 = rnorm(20))
p <- term_penalty(term_build(mcp(~ x1 + x2), dd))
p@params
#> [1] "lambda" "gamma" 
p@params_bounds
#> $lambda
#> [1]   0 Inf
#> 
#> $gamma
#> [1]   1 Inf
#> 

# The derivative starts at lambda and falls linearly to zero at
# gamma * lambda. SCAD's derivative stays at lambda up to t = lambda.
rho1 <- function(t, lambda, gamma) pmax(lambda - t / gamma, 0)
rho1(c(0, 1, 2, 3), lambda = 1, gamma = 2)
#> [1] 1.0 0.5 0.0 0.0

# penalty_kinks() reports the kink at zero and the pair where the second
# derivative breaks.
penalties7::penalty_kinks(p, list(lambda = 1, gamma = 2))
#> [1]  0 -2  2

# The literature's shape is held by default, and `gamma = NULL` estimates it
# over a grid.
term_hyper(mcp(~ x1 + x2))
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$gamma
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> 
term_hyper(mcp(~ x1 + x2, gamma = NULL))
#> list()
term_grid(mcp(~ x1 + x2, gamma = NULL))
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$lambda
#> [1] 25
#> 
#> [[1]]$gamma
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> 

# At or below 1 the objective need not be convex, so it is rejected.
try(mcp(~ x1 + x2, gamma = 1))
#> Error : 'gamma' in 'mcp' must lie strictly inside (1, Inf); it is 1.


# The model is fitted. The data are simulated from a known truth, so the
# estimates below can be read against it.
if (requireNamespace("statmodels7", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(11)
  XX <- matrix(rnorm(150 * 8), 150, 8)
  fd <- data.frame(y = as.numeric(XX %*% c(2, -1.5, 1, rep(0, 5))) +
                     rnorm(150, sd = 0.4))
  fd$X <- XX
  cf <- coef(statmodels7::statmod(y ~ mcp(X),
                                  distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), fd))$mu
  # truth: the first three columns carry 2, -1.5 and 1, the other five
  # nothing. Only lambda is searched: the shape is held at the
  # literature's 3, and `gamma = NULL` would estimate it instead.
  c(round(cf[2:5], 2), kept = sum(cf[-1] != 0))
}
#> mcp.1 mcp.2 mcp.3 mcp.4  kept 
#>  2.00 -1.54  1.02  0.00  5.00
